cells.tense: The listening is open right now, and nothing has been poured into it yet.
cells.ask: Tomorrow, sit down with the person you keep almost-calling and stay at that table for ten minutes without steering. Whatever gets felt in the room is yours to keep.
cells.core:
You feel the shape of a thing before there are words for it — someone's mood crossing the room, a decision that hasn't landed — and you let it come instead of deciding upfront what it is. That isn't passivity. It's contact standing ahead of conclusions, and it's a real skill.

It runs ahead of proof on purpose. That's the next thing to trust: reach for one real moment before you know what it holds — a call, a song you've been avoiding, a conversation you keep circling. Let it pull you forward and don't manage what it stirs. Feeling first, naming later, is the whole move.

cells.tense: You are bracing for what the feeling will cost before it has even arrived.
cells.ask: Before you name what you feel next, say it in one sentence that ends and does not explain. Stop there. Let one piece of your week move on that showing.
cells.core:
You catch the tone of a room before anyone has spoken and let it be what it is. You hear a pause and wait inside it. A half-formed invitation comes and you take it half-formed. None of that needs finishing early.

What happens instead is that you brace for what the feeling will cost before it has arrived. The open moment gets treated as a problem to solve, so you reach past it into a future already decided — rehearsing what you'll say, fixing what hasn't broken, loading a vessel before anything's been poured into it. What goes missing isn't intensity, it's letting one thing stay unanswered. Leave one future you've been rehearsing undecided today.

cells.tense: The feeling used to be something you could trust, and that door has been behind you for a while now.
cells.ask: Each morning this week, put yourself somewhere you can't predict the first ten minutes, and stay fifteen. Let the moment be new instead of already known.
cells.core:
You can walk into a room genuinely unsure what it holds, and the not-knowing can be fine. Someone's face does something and it lands fresh, no file already open. An ordinary morning gets to be a first one.

What happens instead is that you arrive already decided, and the deciding keeps you out of the room. A stranger gets sorted before they've spoken. A morning gets read before you've stepped into it. Nothing terrible happens; nothing reaches you either. What stopped isn't the feeling — it's standing anywhere you can't predict what will land. Fifteen unclaimed minutes in a place you can't call is how it starts again.

cells.tense: You are already feeling your way into things, and you keep describing it as something that just happens to you.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you felt in a situation before you tell them your read on it. Say the felt part first, then let them answer.
cells.core:
You know what you felt about a person before you can argue for it, and you can say so plainly, as yours. You catch what someone needs before they ask, and let that count out loud as your reading of the moment.

It is already running. You catch the mood of a room before anyone speaks; you know how a thing landed before the facts come in. Then you hand the credit to circumstance — a hunch, a good day, whatever was in the air. Take one of those moments this week and put the felt half first, before your explanation of it. What passes between you and the other person is the thing.
